newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, money rates down.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, money rates down.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late Friday trading, with money rates seen easing on lower tax payments, dealers said.
One European bank dealer said sentiment was a bit bearish on dollars in the morning following expensive roll-over costs, but some recovery was seen as swap rates softened.

He said spot rupiah adjusted to central bank fixing as anticipated. Dealers said operators had apparently not sold dollars to the central bank after the fixing because there was not much volume traded below the 2,344.0 level.
Some state banks seemed to have absorbed some dollars from offshore operators at the 2,343.5 and 2,343.75 levels but they appeared to have sold it back to the market.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,344.2/44.4 at 0945 GMT against an opening of 2,343.75/44.75.
"We don't expect any fresh liquidity injection from the central bank next week. However, liquidity expectation suggests a flush supply next week on declining swap rates," one said.
A state bank dealer said he expected the dollar to recover on the back of improved liquidity at the beginning of December and on narrowing interest rate differentials.
He said declining rupiah interest rates, coupled with the three to four points weekly rupiah depreciation and flush liquidity would help strengthen the dollar in the short-term.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,342.5/43.95 and 2,340.00/40.75, respectively.
One swap dealer said declines in swap rates seemed to have brought them close to a low of around seven percent.
"I can remember the recent low for swap premiums was about seven percent. We are now slightly below 7.5 percent. There is not much room to go down further at year-end," he said.
Overnight swap was at 2.35/2.90 and tom/next at 0.50/0.52.
The swap dealer said operators had to square positions at year-end, which may drive up swap rates slightly.
Overnight money fell to 12.0/13.0 percent from a high of 23 percent. It opened at 17.0 percent.
Initial fears over large tax payments, liquidity reports and month-end factors caused overnight rates to rise, but lower than expected tax payments knocked them down again.
One-month swap was at 14.75/15.50, two at 30.5/31.5, three at 43.25/44.00 and six at 87.75/88.75 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,344/2,536 and the conversion rate to 2,344/2,392 on Friday.
